title: [Bug] layer_norm/rms_norm_pre_all_gather 2D core grid path: same wide-row L1 over-allocation, plus a hang at H=1024 W=1024
body:
### Summary

`LayerNormPreAllGather2DProgramFactory` (the `use_2d_core_grid=True` path) carries the same
per-row `x^2` buffer over-allocation that #54697 reports for the default factory, and hits the
same L1 limit at a wide `fp32_dest_acc_en` row.

Separately, and blocking validation of that path, the 2D path **hangs** on an ordinary shape.
Both are described below; the hang is the more serious of the two and may warrant its own issue.

### 1. L1 over-allocation at wide rows

```python
import torch, ttnn
dev = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0)
cfg = ttnn.WormholeComputeKernelConfig(
    math_fidelity=ttnn.MathFidelity.HiFi2, math_approx_mode=False,
    fp32_dest_acc_en=True, packer_l1_acc=True)
x  = torch.randn((1, 1, 32, 4096), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
tt = ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT,
                     device=dev, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
ttnn.rms_norm_pre_all_gather(tt, compute_kernel_config=cfg, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16,
                             use_2d_core_grid=True)
```

Observed on wormhole:

```
Statically allocated dataflow buffers ... grow to 1725632 B
which is beyond max L1 size of 1499136 B
```

Cause is the same as #54697: `intermed0_tiles = Wt * double_buffer_constant` sizes `x^2` at a
full row, doubled, and since #52081 that buffer is fp32 when `fp32_dest_acc_en` is set. The 2D
factory additionally allocates `PRE2D_X2_MERGE` (`cores_y` tiles), which is why its total is
slightly higher than the 1D path's 1684672 B at the same shape.

The 2D compute kernel (`layernorm_pre_allgather_2d.cpp`) has the same fill-to-`Wt`-then-single-
`BulkWaitBulkPop`-reduce structure as the 1D one, so the same adaptive sizing applies: keep the
double buffer where the program fits L1, fall back to a single buffer only where it does not.

Confirmed that works — with adaptive sizing applied to this factory:

| shape (`use_2d_core_grid=True`) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| H=32 W=1024 | runs | runs, PCC 0.9993 |
| H=32 W=2048 | runs | runs, PCC 0.9987 |
| H=32 W=4096 | **fails to allocate** | **runs, PCC 0.9977** |

Note the budget should be L1 above the reserved base
(`l1_size_per_core - get_base_allocator_addr(HalMemType::L1)`), matching what
`validate_dataflow_buffer_region` compares against, and should stay a function of shape/dtypes/
device config only — sizing from `lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address` would make the program
depend on state the program-cache key does not cover.

### 2. Pre-existing hang on a tall ordinary shape

The same call at `H=1024, W=1024` — a width well inside L1, nothing to do with the allocation
above — deadlocks the device:

```
TIMEOUT: device timeout, potential hang detected, the device is unrecoverable
```

This is **not** caused by any buffer-sizing change: it reproduces on an unmodified tree. It is
why the L1 fix above has not been landed for this path — a basic shape deadlocks before the path
can be characterised.

Reproduce by taking the snippet in section 1 and using `(1, 1, 1024, 1024)` for the input shape.
`TT_METAL_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=45` makes it fail fast instead of hanging indefinitely; the
device needs a `tt-smi -r` afterwards.

### Context

`use_2d_core_grid` is opt-in and is not set by any traced model configuration currently in the
sweeps, which is likely why neither problem has been noticed. #54697 / #54698 cover the default
factory only.
